chunks: From him, from Fudayla, from Aban, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Abdillah, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who comes to me seeking a sale, but I do not have what he wants to trade with me until the year. Is it permissible for me to promise him (that I will have it) so that I may purchase goods and then sell them to him? He said, 'Yes.'

key_terms.أَعِدَهُ: I promise him / I give him hope
key_terms.إِلَى السَّنَةِ: Until the year (indicating a period of time)

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to promise a buyer goods you do not currently possess, with the intention of buying them to sell to him?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* validates the practice of promising a future sale (wa'd) when the seller lacks immediate inventory but intends to procure it, a concept foundational to modern Islamic finance structures like *istisna'* and *salam*. Imam al-Sadiq’s affirmative response clarifies that the mere intention to acquire the goods suffices to make the promise binding and permissible, distinguishing it from selling what one does not possess (*bay' al-ma'dum*). This ruling provides scholarly support for deferred delivery contracts in commercial transactions, ensuring market fluidity while adhering to Sharia principles.
